description: Each album's rate is the mean of the per-track ratios Bytes/Milliseconds; compare it with the average of these rates across albums and show the top 10 albums by how far above the average they are.

d.request: For each album (with NULL-AlbumId tracks grouped together), calculate the mean of per-track Bytes/Milliseconds ratios, then rank the top 10 by how far that mean exceeds the overall mean of all per-album means, displaying AlbumId, average UnitPrice, the album's average bytes-per-millisecond rate, and the difference above the all-album average.
d.sql:
WITH track_ratios AS (
  SELECT 
    AlbumId,
    TrackId,
    CAST(Bytes AS DECIMAL) / Milliseconds as bytes_per_ms,
    UnitPrice
  FROM Track
  WHERE Bytes IS NOT NULL AND Milliseconds > 0
),
album_bytes_per_ms AS (
  SELECT 
    AlbumId,
    AVG(bytes_per_ms) as avg_bytes_per_ms
  FROM track_ratios
  GROUP BY AlbumId
),
album_unit_prices AS (
  SELECT 
    AlbumId,
    AVG(UnitPrice) as avg_unit_price
  FROM Track
  GROUP BY AlbumId
),
overall_mean AS (
  SELECT AVG(avg_bytes_per_ms) as overall_mean_bpm
  FROM album_bytes_per_ms
),
album_rankings AS (
  SELECT 
    abpm.AlbumId,
    aup.avg_unit_price,
    abpm.avg_bytes_per_ms,
    abpm.avg_bytes_per_ms - om.overall_mean_bpm as difference_above_mean,
    ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY abpm.avg_bytes_per_ms - om.overall_mean_bpm DESC) as rnk
  FROM album_bytes_per_ms abpm
  INNER JOIN album_unit_prices aup ON abpm.AlbumId = aup.AlbumId
  CROSS JOIN overall_mean om
)
SELECT 
  AlbumId,
  avg_unit_price,
  avg_bytes_per_ms,
  difference_above_mean
FROM album_rankings
WHERE rnk <= 10
ORDER BY difference_above_mean DESC

c.request: Which 10 albums have the highest bytes-per-millisecond rate compared with the average across all albums? Group tracks by `AlbumId`, with tracks that have no album id counted together as one group. For each album, show the album id, the average track `UnitPrice`, the album's average bytes per millisecond, and how far it is above the all-album average. Ignore missing values, don't round, and sort by that difference, largest first. Each album's rate is the mean of the per-track ratios Bytes/Milliseconds; compare it with the average of these rates across albums and show the top 10 albums by how far above the average they are.
c.sql:
WITH track_ratios AS (
  SELECT 
    AlbumId,
    UnitPrice,
    CAST(Bytes AS DECIMAL(20,10)) / CAST(Milliseconds AS DECIMAL(20,10)) AS rate
  FROM Track
  WHERE Bytes IS NOT NULL 
    AND Milliseconds IS NOT NULL 
    AND Milliseconds > 0
),
album_stats AS (
  SELECT 
    AlbumId,
    AVG(UnitPrice) AS AvgUnitPrice,
    AVG(rate) AS AvgBytesPerMillisecond
  FROM track_ratios
  GROUP BY AlbumId
),
with_global_avg AS (
  SELECT 
    *,
    AVG(AvgBytesPerMillisecond) OVER () AS GlobalAvg
  FROM album_stats
)
SELECT 
  AlbumId,
  AvgUnitPrice,
  AvgBytesPerMillisecond,
  AvgBytesPerMillisecond - GlobalAvg AS DifferenceFromAverage
FROM with_global_avg
ORDER BY DifferenceFromAverage DESC
LIMIT 10;

b.request: Each album's bytes-per-millisecond rate is the mean of its tracks' individual Bytes/Milliseconds ratios; show the 10 albums whose rate is furthest above the mean of all such per-album rates.
b.sql:
WITH track_ratios AS (
  SELECT 
    AlbumId,
    Bytes * 1.0 / Milliseconds as ratio
  FROM Track
  WHERE Bytes IS NOT NULL AND Milliseconds > 0
),
album_rates AS (
  SELECT 
    AlbumId,
    AVG(ratio) as rate
  FROM track_ratios
  GROUP BY AlbumId
),
stats AS (
  SELECT 
    AVG(rate) as mean_rate
  FROM album_rates
)
SELECT 
  Album.AlbumId,
  Album.Title,
  album_rates.rate,
  album_rates.rate - stats.mean_rate as difference_from_mean
FROM album_rates
JOIN Album ON album_rates.AlbumId = Album.AlbumId
CROSS JOIN stats
ORDER BY difference_from_mean DESC
LIMIT 10;
b.raw: Each album's bytes-per-millisecond rate is the mean of its tracks' individual Bytes/Milliseconds ratios; show the 10 albums whose rate is furthest above the mean of all such per-album rates.

a.request: Group tracks by `AlbumId` (tracks with no album id together count as one group). For each group, show the album id, the average track `UnitPrice`, the album's bytes-per-millisecond rate (the average of each track's `Bytes` ÷ `Milliseconds`), and how far that rate is above the average rate across all albums. Ignore missing values in averages and don't round. List the 10 albums with the largest difference, largest first.
a.sql:
WITH track_rates AS (
  SELECT 
    AlbumId,
    CAST(Bytes AS DECIMAL) / Milliseconds as rate,
    UnitPrice
  FROM Track
  WHERE Bytes IS NOT NULL
),
album_stats AS (
  SELECT 
    AlbumId,
    AVG(UnitPrice) as avg_unit_price,
    AVG(rate) as avg_rate
  FROM track_rates
  GROUP BY AlbumId
),
overall_avg_rate AS (
  SELECT AVG(rate) as global_avg_rate
  FROM track_rates
)
SELECT 
  a.AlbumId,
  a.avg_unit_price,
  a.avg_rate,
  a.avg_rate - o.global_avg_rate as difference_from_average
FROM album_stats a
CROSS JOIN overall_avg_rate o
ORDER BY difference_from_average DESC
LIMIT 10;
